origins.section: A Disjunction Written as Big-M Switches Each Disjunct With Its Own Binary
The Hull Gives Each Disjunct Its Own Copy of the Variables
The Hull Is Tighter but Bigger, and for One Variable a Tight Big-M Already Is the Hull

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-sequencing-m: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-sequencing-m: $`M`$ must cover the largest value of $`s_i + d_i - s_j`$: $`s_i`$ at its upper bound $`H - d_i`$ and $`s_j`$ at its lower bound 0
recorded.prompt:q-hull-lp: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-hull-lp: When $`y_{ij}`$ is a fraction $`\lambda`$, the $`a`$ copies describe a valid "$`i`$ first" schedule scaled by $`\lambda`$, the $`b`$ copies a valid "$`j`$ first" schedule scaled by $`1 - \lambda`$, and the starts are their sum: a weighted average of two real schedules.
recorded.prompt:q-when-hull: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-when-hull: **One variable, intervals:** a tight big-M is already the hull. Use it; it is smaller.
